data.content_ref: inline:The target's evidence criterion ('Temporal-Spatial Coincidence') fails the problem's second requirement: to distinguish failures that are TRULY independent from those that merely APPEAR uncorrelated until a shared cause is found. The target explicitly defines its mechanism around spikes coinciding with a shared external stimulus, but that only catches correlated failures whose shared cause produces a temporally coincident signature. It does not supply evidence that would affirm TRUE independence: a long record with no coincident spike is necessary but not sufficient, because a slow-acting or staggered shared cause (which the target itself concedes as a countercondition) produces exactly the same non-coincident failure record as genuinely independent Poisson failures. By the target's own stated countercondition, two qualitatively different causal realities (true independence vs. masked/staggered correlation) yield observationally indistinguishable evidence under its proposed test. Thus the evidence the target names does not distinguish the two cases the problem asks it to distinguish; it only detects one of them.
